business: Village Basket (working name): daily pooled grocery run with a village pickup point, Amchit and the Jbeil hill villages
by_segment: Amchit-centre household, 5 to 6 minutes by car from Spinneys, Tawfeer MAX and Le Charcutier in Jbeil
Hill-village household (Bejjeh, Ghalboun, Aabaydat or Kfoun), 20 to 25 minutes by car from the Jbeil supermarkets
Older person or couple who rarely or never drives
Comfortable family on two salaries or remittances from abroad
why_not: I already go down to Jbeil once a week and fill the boot, and I see the prices with my own eyes. Sending a list before 2 p.m. every time is a hassle, and I would be trusting strangers with my cash and my groceries.
I already drive down to Jbeil every Saturday for the big shop, and the dekkene owner is my neighbour and lets me pay at the end of the month. I don't need someone else doing my shopping.

I already grab bread and labneh at the dekkene every morning and sometimes put it on the tab. Ordering by 2 p.m. and driving to a pickup point between 6 and 8 for a bag is a hassle, and I don't know who these people are.
Spinneys and Tawfeer are five minutes from my house, so I can go myself and see the price on the shelf. I don't see why I'd hand my list to a stranger and take their word for the receipt.
I already run a tab at the dekkene and it costs me nothing extra. A list before 2 p.m. and a trip to a pickup point between 6 and 8 for a $2 fee on top, that is more hassle than what I do now.

I already follow the Tawfeer and supermarket offers myself and stock up when there is a deal, and Jbeil is only 5 or 6 minutes by car. If I still have to go and collect the bag at their hour, in a pickup point, I save almost nothing and pay $2 for it.

I want to pick my own vegetables and meat, and I would not hand that to someone I don't know. I already get bread and labneh at the dekkene most days and do my big shop in Jbeil on Saturday, so this doesn't fill a gap for me.
I choose my own vegetables, fruit and meat, and I am not letting a stranger pick them for me. I already drive to Jbeil on Saturday for the big shop, so I do not need this.
I'm 65, I have my tab at the dekkene and I'm in the Jbeil supermarkets anyway when I go. Paying $2 a bag to have someone shop for me, then driving to a pickup point in the evening, saves me nothing.

I'm five minutes from Spinneys and Tawfeer and I already fill the boot once a week, and for the small stuff I have my tab at the dekkene. I don't need someone else to do my shopping and then drive to a pickup point to get it.

I already stop at the supermarket on my way home from work, so this saves me nothing in time, and $2 a bag is real money when every dollar counts. I would not trust that the pooling saves more than the fee.
I already pass through Jbeil on my commute and do the big shop there on Saturday, so I can compare prices myself. Another $2 a bag on top of groceries is money I don't have to spare.
why_yes: We have no car right now, so getting to Spinneys or Tawfeer in Jbeil is a real problem for me. A bag waiting in the village for $2 on top of till prices is cheaper than paying someone to drive me, so I would try it for dry goods and packs.

We have no car right now, so getting to Jbeil for a shop is a real hassle, and a $2 fee for someone to buy it and have it in my village is less than a taxi or asking a favour. I'd try it for stock-up lists, not every day.

With no car in the house, getting a bag of shopping up from Jbeil is a hassle, so a pickup point in my own village that I can walk to is useful. I would try it for the heavy things like oil, rice and cartons, not every day.
flip: A neighbour I know and trust who has used it for a month and shows me the receipt next to the bag, and the fee dropped to $1 or free on a big weekly bag.

If I could send a photo of what I want, or they sent me a picture before buying, and I could refuse what I don't like at pickup.
Delivery to my door with no fee, or proof that the carton prices come out clearly cheaper than what I pay at Tawfeer, enough to cover the fee.
